newsitem.title: INDIA: Hongkong Bank cuts Indian prime rates to 17 pct.
newsitem.headline: Hongkong Bank cuts Indian prime rates to 17 pct.

text.p: Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corporation Ltd reduced its Indian prime lending rate to 17.0 percent per annum from 18.0 percent with immediate effect, the bank's Bombay office said on Wednesday.

"The reduction is in response to the monetary policy for the second half of 1996/97 announced on October 19, which clearly signals a lowering of real interest rates in the economy," the bank said in a statement.

It said key policy measures ananounced by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) -- reduction in cash reserve ratio (CRR) for banks, lowering of the cap on short-term deposits and permitting banks to onlend FCNR funds to corporates in foreign currency -- have already resulted in easier money market conditions.
Hongkong Bank listed the following changes that prompted its rate cut:

- "Call rates have fallen to 8.5 percent from 9.5 percent and the dollar six-month swap rate has softened to 7.25 percent from 8.5 percent. We expect these rates to decline further in the coming weeks.
- The stable credit demand of the private sector, plus a growth in the banking sectors deposit base.
- The inflation rate continues to remain under control as measured by the wholesale price index, currently at 6.45 percent.
- The Hongkong Bank's own short-term liquidity position."

The statement quoted the banks chief executive officer in India, Diccon Pullen, as saying: "The major initiatives contained in the RBI's monetary policy will result in enhanced short-term liquidity and a reduction in the cost of resources to the banking sector."
"The cut in our PLR was possible, partly due to the lower cost of resources and partly due to our expectations of lower real interest rates in the future," he said.
